authoring: Frozen source-defined native predicate after reading the complete modern workflow and original run-identity metadata, before inspecting any original job log, artifact or native result. Historical source differences require explicit profiles, not backdated modern acceptance.
goal: Verify that the Codex engine can use GitHub remote MCP to retrieve three open repository issues, or respect an explicitly returned integrity-policy content filter without bypass.

selection.population: All nine surviving pre-cutoff workflow run identities in a complete 100-item API page, not proof that each started an agent

acceptance.nativeAccess: Count distinct source-bound Codex run-attempts with an independently captured, correlated native GitHub remote MCP list_issues invocation and non-error returned result. Direct gh/api/shell fallback, assistant prose, echoed examples, tool declarations and job success do not qualify.
acceptance.openIssueReadback: Count distinct independently returned repository issue identities with concrete numbers, titles and OPEN/open state from an accepted native call requesting three issues from github/gh-aw. All three must be witnessed to establish the source-defined three-issue component. Filtered or missing contents remain unknown, not fabricated issue readbacks.
acceptance.filteredAccess: A concrete independently returned native integrity-policy filter with a concrete found count is an expected access-policy facet, never proof of issue-content readback or permission to bypass.
acceptance.binding: Preserve original public repository identity, run/attempt/job metadata, exact-head editable and compiled sources and protected provider/tool result originals. Verify execution identity, call correlation, host/path and timestamps where the native claim depends on them.
acceptance.deduplication: One accepted native-access observation per stable run-attempt identity. Native issue identities are deduplicated within their opportunity; repeated safety/capability checks are not fresh repository repairs.

limitations: Native access, returned issue bytes, policy-filter behavior, full goal completion and workflow-linked delivered contribution remain separate.
Absent, expired, skipped or incompatible original evidence is unknown, not zero accepted work or a proved failed tool.
No threshold, aggregate quality score, dollar value, cost, exclusive causation or deployment authority is inferred.
Current API state is acquisition-time evidence, not reconstructed historical issue state.
